title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Volodymyr Mnih and collaborators submitted 'Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning' on February 4, 2016. The paper presents asynchronous variants of four reinforcement-learning algorithms and reports that its asynchronous actor-critic variant was the best-performing method in the study.
significance: A documented deep-reinforcement-learning research milestone for asynchronous parallel actor-learners and the asynchronous actor-critic method commonly associated with A3C.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the February 4 2016 submission date, title, authors, and the paper's asynchronous deep-reinforcement-learning framework. The ICML 2016 PMLR proceedings independently establish the paper's conference publication and describe the asynchronous actor-critic variant as the best-performing method reported in the paper. No invention date, development start, development geography, institutional affiliation, ancestry, influence, causality, universal-priority claim, or relationship is inferred.
